 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. It was another stellar weekend of college football and parity is alive and well. After Miami went down against Notre Dame , there are just two undefeated teams left in the sport: Utah and UCLA. Both of those teams played this weekend and took care of business.
 Utah beat BYU at home in the Holy War, while the Bruins traveled to Minnesota to beat the Gophers. Obviously, there were other games to know this past weekend with seven ranked matchups
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Georgia crushed Ole Miss, Texas beat Missouri, Ohio State lost to Oregon, and Alabama dominated LSU, among others.
 MORE: Predicting College Football Playoff field after Week 10: Georgia claims top spot 
 Stock up: Utah makes argument for No. 1 ranking
 Nov 7, 2026; Salt Lake City, Utah, USA; Utah Utes quarterback Devon Dampier (4) reacts after scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter against the Brigham Young Cougars at Rice-Eccles Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
 Utah about lost the home game on Saturday. The Utes got out to a quick 14-0 lead, but BYU battled back. The Cougars would score 20 unanswered points in the game to take the lead, but Utah's defense made one too many plays. The Utes intercepted Bear Bachmeier four times and won 28-20.
 The Utes are now 9-0 and have beaten both ranked teams on their schedule. Utah has taken care of both Houston and BYU and they are making a strong case to become the No. 1 team on Tuesday night. Will they pass Georgia? Likely not, but a win next week against Arizona could propel the Utes up.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Stock down: Ohio State's CFP hopes appear finished
 Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day celebrates a touchdown by running back Bo Jackson (25) during the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Nov. 7, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
 Ohio State is now 0-2 with Luke Fahey at quarterback. Julian Sayin isn't likely coming back this season and the Buckeyes are either going to stick with Fahey or move to former five-star Tavien St. Clair, who hasn't started for a reason.
 The Buckeyes aren't just not scoring points, but their defense has regressed. Ohio State had a 14-0 cushion, but the Ducks turned up their offense with Dylan Raiola behind center. Oregon would win the game 41-28 in Columbus and Ohio State now has three losses.
 It's not impossible to make the playoff with three losses, but the Buckeyes are a shell of what they are supposed to be. Michigan doesn't appear like it can challenge Ohio State, but next week's game against Northwestern certainly isn't a gimme.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Stock up: Notre Dame gets statement win
 Nov 7, 2026; South Bend, Indiana, USA; Notre Dame Fighting Irish quarterback CJ Carr (13) and quarterback Noah Grubbs (10) warm up before the game against the Miami Hurricanes at Notre Dame Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Michael Caterina-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
 The College Football Playoff committee told Notre Dame everything it needed to know last Tuesday. Ranking the Irish at No. 11 told them they couldn't lose the game to Miami, or they would miss the playoff for the second season in a row.
 Without Miami star Malachi Toney, Notre Dame was able to capitalize enough to win a stellar game, 31-24. Notre Dame has now split both of its tough games this season. The Irish lost to BYU on the road and they've taken down Miami.
 Barring an upset this season, Notre Dame will comfortably make the playoff and now the only question is if it will get a first-round bye.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Stock down: Lane Kiffin's first season isn't as expected
 Tigers Head Coach Lane Kiffin, The LSU Tigers take on Alabama. November 7, 2026; Baton Rouge, LA, USA; at Tiger Stadium. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
 When Lane Kiffin left Ole Miss prior to the playoff last season, he took a lot of staff with him and he hit the transfer portal harder than anyone. Sam Leavitt was supposed to be a great fit with Kiffin at LSU, but the Tigers' season has been mixed.
 LSU has six wins and it's lost all three of its biggest games. The Tigers were just throttled at home against Alabama, 31-13. Kiffin's offseason antics put LSU under the microscope and with games against both Texas and Tennessee still on the schedule, it's possible the Tigers have five losses this season under Kiffin.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Stock up: Oregon remains alive with another big win
 Oregon head coach Dan Lanning, left, talks to Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola before a touchdown play as the Oregon Ducks face the Ohio State Buckeyes on Nov. 7, 2026, at Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
 Oregon is suddenly alive and well. Despite being without star quarterback Dante Moore, a bevy of injuries, and firing their offensive coordinator, the Ducks have found an answer and they've won back-to-back impressive games. A win over Northwestern last weekend and a statement win over Ohio State in Columbus this weekend.
 The Ducks are tied for third in the conference, but need a few things to go in their favor to make the Big Ten Championship Game, along with winning out. Here is Oregon's last three games: vs. Michigan, at Michigan State, and vs. Washington.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement All three should be wins and the Ducks would have a strong argument to make the playoff.
 Stock down: Kyle Whittingham
 Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham walks up the tunnel after 13-6 loss to Indiana in overtime at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
 This wasn't what it was supposed to look like when Kyle Whittingham came to Michigan. The Wolverines suffered an embarrassing 15-6 loss to rival Michigan State on Saturday, and the Spartans had two wins entering the rivalry game.
 Michigan's offense has only regressed under Whittingham and offensive coordinator Jason Beck. The Wolverines are on the brink of missing a bowl game. With a 5-4 record, the Wolverines' final three games are: at Oregon, vs. UCLA, and at Ohio State. Not sure where that final win is at.
 Whittingham is on the brink of being one-and-done.
